heard: campus outcasts blew up a lab and built NASA's Premier Space Center. In 1936, Caltech graduate student Frank Melina teamed up with self-taught rocketeers Jack Parsons and Edward Foreman. Their hazardous motor tests caused dangerous explosions, earning the group the campus nickname Suicide Squad. After blasting a hole through a wall, the squad was banished from Caltech to a dry riverbed called Arroyo Seco. Working outdoors, They built take-off rockets for propeller aircraft, proposing the name Jet Propulsion Laboratory in 1943. In 1958, JPL launched America's first satellite, Explorer 1, before transferring to the newly created NASA. That former riverbed camp went on to manage Voyager 1, the first human craft in interstellar space. America's entire planetary exploration program began after a campus explosion.
